As for its existence, black holes slowly "evaporate" through a process called Hawking radiation. Matter/antimatter particle pairs pop into existence then instantly annihilate each other all the time. If this happens right on the event horizon of a black hole, one particle will fall in while the other escapes, resulting in a loss of energy within the black hole, which translates directly to a loss of mass.

This is a pretty slow process that doesn't even happen unless the temperature of the cosmic microwave background is lower than the temperature of the black hole, and SGRA * is pretty damn cold (0.00000000000001 degrees Kelvin), so assuming my figures and math are correct... it'll be around 1300000000000000000000000 years before it even starts to evaporate. SGRA * is also unimaginably massive, so even once that process begins it'll be countless years before it evaporates into nothing.

That black hole will outlast this galaxy and everything in it by several orders of magnitude.

Apart from Anno series, what would you recommend for person who likes building and economy aspect of RTS over the military/fighting one?

I've actually been obsessed with Offworld Trading Company recently. It is a strictly economic game, no units at all.

The single player is fun but the multiplayer is where the real fun is had.

I would wait till the encore sale to see if you can pick it up for $20. It is early access but the lead designer is the same lead designer from Civ IV.

The Tropico series' more recent iterations might be satisfying, but the scale is quite different (individual units).

Also, have a look at Banished.

Yea, I was going to suggest tropico as well. It is mostly city building with little combat in Tropico 2 and 4 but when combat does happen it can be very serious. In tropico 5 combat plays a bigger part but is overall a very good citybuilding series.
